You can kill a Python process on Linux using the `kill` command. First, identify the process ID (PID) of the Python process using tools like `ps` or `top`. Then, use `kill <PID>` to send a termination signal. If that doesn't work, you can use `kill -9 <PID>` which forces immediate termination. Be aware that `-9` can lead to data loss if the process doesn't have a chance to clean up.
